results.prompt: Make a mono green storm deck in Premodern.
results.text:
I built a mono-green storm deck that wins with **Hunting Pack**. It's an original design (a brew). It borrows the elf engine and mana style from Premodern Elves, which shows up in 33 recent lists. Every one of those lists splashes another color, though, and none of them uses storm.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Llanowar Elves
- 4 Fyndhorn Elves
- 4 Priest of Titania
- 4 Quirion Ranger
- 4 Wirewood Symbiote
- 4 Multani's Acolyte
- 3 Wirewood Channeler
- 2 Deranged Hermit
- 4 Hunting Pack
- 3 Survival of the Fittest
- 2 Concordant Crossroads
- 4 Lotus Petal
- 2 Land Grant
- 4 Gaea's Cradle
- 12 Forest

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Naturalize
- 3 Tormod's Crypt
- 3 Xantid Swarm
- 2 Masticore
- 2 Ravenous Baloth
- 2 Caller of the Claw

**The plan**
Premodern only has two green storm cards: Hunting Pack and Sprouting Vines. The deck is built around Hunting Pack, an instant that costs 5GG and makes a 4/4 Beast, plus one more Beast for every spell cast before it that turn.
- Cast lots of cheap elves and free spells in one turn, then cast Hunting Pack. With six spells before it you get seven 4/4s.
- With **Concordant Crossroads** (G: all creatures have haste) in play, new elves can tap for mana right away and the Beasts can attack the turn they're made.
- Without Crossroads, you still end up with a large army of Beasts on the table.

**Why these cards**
- **Mana for the big turn:** Priest of Titania makes G for each elf, Wirewood Channeler makes X mana for each elf, and Gaea's Cradle makes G for each creature. Quirion Ranger untaps one of them by returning a Forest to your hand.
- **Adding to the spell count:** Lotus Petal costs 0, so it's a free spell. Land Grant is free if you have no lands in hand. Wirewood Symbiote can return a Multani's Acolyte to your hand. Recasting it for GG adds a spell, draws a card and untaps one of your mana creatures.
- **Survival of the Fittest** turns spare dorks into whichever creature you need, like Channeler or Hermit. It can't find Hunting Pack, because Pack isn't a creature.
- **Deranged Hermit** is the backup plan: it adds four Squirrels, which boost Gaea's Cradle and can win in combat.

**The mana**
The deck runs 16 lands, all Forests or Cradles because Quirion Ranger needs Forests. The deck checker pointed out that Elves lists average 19 lands, so this is a deliberate choice:
- You also have 4 Lotus Petal and 2 Land Grant.
- 12 elves cost one mana.
- The average card costs 2.14.
- Real Elves lists need extra lands for their splash colors and Armageddon, and this deck has neither.

**Honest odds**
With no mulligans, you have a 56.6% chance of drawing Hunting Pack naturally by turn 5. The Acolyte draws raise that. If it doesn't show up, play Hermit and attack.

**Sideboarding against the current meta**
- **Enchantress (12.5%):** bring in 3 Naturalize and 3 Xantid Swarm. Cut Crossroads and a Land Grant, plus 2 to 4 weaker dorks so the deck stays at 60.
- **Stiflenought and UB Psychatog (blue counterspell decks):** bring in 3 Xantid Swarm. When Swarm attacks, the opponent can't cast spells that turn, so attack before your big turn. Cut Land Grants and a Survival.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in 2 Masticore and 2 Ravenous Baloth. Cut both Crossroads, because it also gives *their* creatures haste, and some Land Grants or Petals.
- **Hermit Druid Combo:** bring in 3 Tormod's Crypt, which exiles a graveyard for 0. Add Swarms too.
- **Terrageddon:** Your 1-mana elves help you recover from land destruction. After sweepers, Caller of the Claw (Flash) makes a 2/2 Bear for each of your creatures that died that turn.

**What I couldn't verify**
These lists have never been played in tournaments. The only results I could check were for the individual cards: Hunting Pack appeared in 4 lists in the last 90 days, and Concordant Crossroads and Wirewood Channeler in none. The power level and the sideboard plan come from my reasoning, not from match data.

results.prompt: Build a Replenish deck in Premodern that doesn't play blue.
results.text:
I built a white-black Replenish deck with no blue cards and submitted it as a **brew**. Nobody in recent results plays Replenish without blue, so this is a new list. The mana and removal come from the standard white-blue Replenish deck, which is 4.8% of the current field.

## Main deck (60)
**The combo (24 cards)**
- 4 Replenish
- 4 Opalescence
- 4 Parallax Wave
- 4 Lion's Eye Diamond
- 4 Zombie Infestation
- 3 Insidious Dreams
- 1 Cabal Therapy

**Interaction and card draw (12 cards)**
- 4 Swords to Plowshares
- 3 Seal of Cleansing
- 3 Abeyance
- 2 Phyrexian Arena

**Lands (24)**
- 10 Plains
- 4 Swamp
- 4 Ancient Tomb
- 4 Caves of Koilos
- 2 Tainted Field

## Sideboard (15)
- 3 Exalted Angel
- 3 Defense Grid
- 2 Duress
- 2 Solitary Confinement
- 2 Tormod's Crypt
- 2 Circle of Protection: Red
- 1 Wrath of God

## The plan
Put enchantments into your graveyard, then cast Replenish ({3}{W}) to bring them all back at once. Opalescence turns your other enchantments into creatures, each with power and toughness equal to its mana value. Parallax Wave (a 4/4 under Opalescence) exiles blockers, and your board of animated enchantments wins the game. If you draw the pieces naturally, you can also just cast Opalescence and Parallax Wave.

## Why these cards
**Replacing blue's cards.** The blue lists rely on Attunement, Frantic Search and Intuition. All of them are blue, so I replaced them:
- **Lion's Eye Diamond:** cast Replenish, then use the Diamond's mana to pay for it. The Diamond makes you discard your hand, which throws your enchantments into the graveyard right before Replenish returns them. With a Plains and a hand full of enchantments, that can happen on turn 1.
- **Zombie Infestation:** discard two cards at any time to make a 2/2 Zombie. It's also an enchantment, so Replenish returns it.
- **Insidious Dreams:** an instant that costs {3}{B}. Discard X cards, then put X cards from your library on top in any order. Cast it at the end of your opponent's turn, discard your enchantments, and stack Replenish and Lion's Eye Diamond on top.
- **Cabal Therapy:** it targets any player, so you can name your own enchantment to discard every copy. You can also use it to take a key card from your opponent.

**Other cards:**
- **Abeyance** is white, and the blue lists already play it in 72% of decks. It protects your combo turn and draws a card.
- **Phyrexian Arena** replaces some of blue's card draw.
- **Seal of Cleansing** destroys an artifact or enchantment by sacrificing itself, which also puts it in your graveyard for Replenish.

**The odds:** by turn 4 on the play, you have a 74% chance of seeing Replenish or Insidious Dreams. You have a 79% chance of seeing Lion's Eye Diamond or Zombie Infestation, and a 57% chance of both. That's less consistent than the blue lists, which are built around Intuition. Without it, you're relying on extra copies and the option to hard-cast your enchantments.

## The mana
The deck has 24 lands, close to the blue lists' 25. Lion's Eye Diamond adds extra mana when you combo. There are 16 white sources (10 Plains, 4 Caves of Koilos, 2 Tainted Field) for your WW and W costs, and 10 black sources (4 Swamp, 4 Caves, 2 Tainted Field) for Infestation, Dreams and Arena. Tainted Field only makes coloured mana if you control a Swamp. Ancient Tomb gives you {C}{C} for turn-2 Opalescence or Wave, as it does in 98% of the blue lists. The deck check passed with no errors; its only note was the expected one that the deck has fewer blue sources than other Replenish lists.

## Sideboarding against the current field
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in Circle of Protection: Red, Solitary Confinement and Wrath of God. Take out Cabal Therapy, the Arenas and Ancient Tombs to cut your own life loss. Solitary Confinement prevents all damage to you, and its discard cost each upkeep feeds Replenish.
- **Stiflenought, UB Psychatog and Standstill:** bring in Defense Grid and Duress to stop counterspells and Stifle. Take out Swords to Plowshares and Seal of Cleansing.
- **Terrageddon and Moneyball Black:** bring in Duress and Defense Grid. Exalted Angel gives you a creature threat that doesn't depend on the graveyard.
- **Hermit Druid Combo:** bring in Tormod's Crypt and Duress. Crypt targets one player's graveyard, so it won't hurt yours.
- **Enchantress and the mirror:** keep all the Seals. Exalted Angel gives you a second way to win after they board in graveyard hate.

## Things I couldn't verify
- **Rules interactions:** two of these are standard but still worth checking with a judge before a tournament:
  - Paying for Replenish with Lion's Eye Diamond after it's on the stack.
  - Using Parallax Wave on itself once Opalescence makes it a creature. When the Wave leaves the battlefield, it returns with fresh counters, while the creatures it exiled in the meantime stay exiled.
- **Untested choices:** Insidious Dreams has no recent tournament results, and none of these card counts have been tested in matches.
- **Graveyard hate:** Tormod's Crypt is in 44.6% of recent lists, and every graveyard-based deck is weak to it. Your backups are hard-casting enchantments and Exalted Angel.

results.prompt: Build a Modern deck around Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact.
results.text:
**First, a problem: Tainted Pact isn't legal in Modern.** The card lookup lists it as "not legal." It was printed in Odyssey and never reprinted in a Modern-legal set, so the deck can't be built as asked.

The closest legal version is **Inverter of Truth + Thassa's Oracle** in the same Dimir (blue-black) colors. Inverter does Pact's job. Its text: "When this creature enters, exile all cards from your library face down, then shuffle all cards from your graveyard into your library." If your graveyard is empty or small, your library ends up empty or tiny. Then Oracle wins: it wins if your devotion to blue is at least the number of cards left in your library, and Oracle alone gives you 2. This also removes Pact's biggest limit: you don't need a deck with only one copy of each card, so you get 4 copies of each combo piece. I submitted it as a **brew**.

**Main deck (60)**
- **Combo (12):** 4 Inverter of Truth, 4 Thassa's Oracle, 1 Jace, Wielder of Mysteries, 3 Tormod's Crypt
- **Speed and tutors (5):** 3 Talisman of Dominance, 2 Grim Tutor
- **Discard (5):** 4 Thoughtseize, 1 Inquisition of Kozilek
- **Removal (5):** 4 Fatal Push, 1 Cut Down
- **Counterspells (5):** 3 Counterspell, 2 Drown in the Loch
- **Card draw (6):** 4 Consider, 2 Opt
- **Lands (22):** 4 Watery Grave, 4 Darkslick Shores, 4 Polluted Delta, 2 Gloomlake Verge, 2 Undercity Sewers, 1 Drowned Catacomb, 1 Otawara, Soaring City, 1 Bojuka Bog, 2 Island, 1 Swamp

**Sideboard (15):** 2 Force of Negation, 2 Mystical Dispute, 2 Consign to Memory, 2 Spell Pierce, 2 Sheoldred's Edict, 1 Cut Down, 2 Hurkyl's Recall, 1 Pithing Needle, 1 Engineered Explosives

**The plan:** Use cheap discard, removal and counterspells to protect yourself while you find Inverter and Oracle. There are two ways to win:
- **One turn, 6 mana:** Cast Inverter. While its effect is waiting to resolve, sacrifice Tormod's Crypt (or play Bojuka Bog) to exile your graveyard. Your library ends up with 0 cards. Then cast Oracle and win.
- **Over two turns:** Cast Inverter when your graveyard has 3 or fewer cards. You draw 1 on your next turn, so 2 or fewer remain, and Oracle wins.

**Why the key cards:**
- **Tormod's Crypt and Bojuka Bog** control how many cards end up back in your library. Only empty your library when you can win that same turn. Otherwise you lose on your next draw.
- **Jace, Wielder of Mysteries** is a backup win: once Inverter has emptied your library, any draw wins. Jace's +1 can make you mill 2 to speed this up.
- **Talisman of Dominance** lets you cast Inverter on turn 3, or both pieces on turn 5.
- **Grim Tutor** finds whichever piece you're missing.

**Mana:** I copied the mana base from Modern's Frog deck, the most-played blue-black deck: Watery Grave, Polluted Delta, Darkslick Shores, Gloomlake Verge and Undercity Sewers. You have 20 blue and 19 black sources, enough for both Oracle (needs two blue) and Inverter (needs two black). I'm running 22 lands, while the deck check suggests 20.1. That's on purpose, because the one-turn kill needs 6 mana.

**Sideboarding against the current field:**
- **Broodscale Combo (14.4% of the field):** bring in Consign to Memory, Pithing Needle, Hurkyl's Recall and Engineered Explosives.
- **Affinity:** bring in Hurkyl's Recall and Consign to Memory.
- **Prowess, Energy and Devoted Druid:** bring in Sheoldred's Edict, Cut Down and Explosives. Take out Counterspell and Opt.
- **Storm, Goryo's Vengeance and Living End:** bring in Force of Negation and Spell Pierce. Consign to Memory also helps against Living End.
- **Frog and control decks:** bring in Mystical Dispute and Spell Pierce. Take out some removal.

**Honest odds:** If you never mulligan, you'll have Inverter plus a second piece (Oracle, Jace or Grim Tutor) by turn 5 on the play about 39.5% of the time. You'll have Inverter or a Grim Tutor by turn 4 about 61% of the time. Card draw spells raise both numbers. This is a slower, more fragile combo than the one you asked for. The card is legal, but recent results show no Inverter decks in Modern, so this deck hasn't been tested in tournaments.

**Things I couldn't fix:**
- Spoils of the Vault isn't a substitute. It exiles cards like Pact does, but you lose 1 life for each one, which would kill you.
- Leveler also exiles your library, but it costs 5 and doesn't put your graveyard back, so I left it out.
- If you want the real Tainted Pact + Oracle combo, you need a format where Pact is legal. I didn't build for one because you specified Modern.

results.prompt: I want a Modern Merfolk deck that can beat the current top decks.
results.text:
I built a mono-blue Merfolk deck that hits hard early and holds up a cheap counter or bounce spell each turn. It's tuned for Modern's current top decks, which right now are Broodscale Combo (14.4% of the field), Prowess (9.9%), Energy, Blink and Affinity.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Aether Vial
- 4 Tide Shaper
- 4 Lord of Atlantis
- 4 Master of the Pearl Trident
- 4 Silvergill Adept
- 4 Vodalian Hexcatcher
- 4 Harbinger of the Seas
- 4 Svyelun of Sea and Sky
- 3 Tishana's Tidebinder
- 4 Flare of Denial
- 4 Sink into Stupor
- 1 Snapback
- 4 Cavern of Souls
- 7 Island
- 3 Mutavault
- 2 Otawara, Soaring City

**Sideboard (15)**
- 4 Chalice of the Void
- 4 Consign to Memory
- 3 Force of Negation
- 2 Subtlety
- 2 Dismember

**The plan**
Play cheap Merfolk off Aether Vial and Cavern of Souls, then stack the creatures that pump the team (Lord, Master, Hexcatcher). Harbinger and Tide Shaper turn the opponent's lands into Islands, so your Lords' islandwalk makes your attackers unblockable. Free or cheap interaction like Flare of Denial and Sink into Stupor stops the opponent long enough for you to win, usually by turn 4 or 5.

**Why the key cards**
- **Harbinger of the Seas:** "Nonbasic lands are Islands" shuts off Broodscale's Eldrazi Temple and Urza's Saga, and Eldrazi Tron's lands too. It also turns on islandwalk against almost any deck. Saga should be sacrificed under Harbinger, the same way it is under Blood Moon. That's my reading of the rules, not something the tools showed me.
- **Tishana's Tidebinder (my main change):** it has flash and can be put in off Vial at 3. It counters one activated or triggered ability, and if that ability came from a creature or artifact, that permanent loses all its abilities while Tidebinder stays. That stops Basking Broodscale and Blade of the Bloodchief combo triggers, the cast trigger on Emrakul, the Promised End, and Saga's final chapter. It also gives you another Merfolk body.
- **Lord, Master and Hexcatcher:** with 12 of them, you have an 88.7% chance to see one by turn 3 on the play. Hexcatcher also has flash and can sacrifice a Merfolk to tax a noncreature spell.
- **Svyelun:** draws a card each time it attacks and gives your other Merfolk ward 1, which is good against Prowess's burn and Energy's removal.
- **Flare of Denial, Sink into Stupor and Snapback:** you can cast all three without spending mana or tapping out on your own turn. Sink can also be played as a land when you need one.

**Mana**
You have 16 lands plus Sink into Stupor, which can be played as a land. That matches the real Merfolk lists (17.4 lands on average). The checker's generic suggestion of 20.5 lands doesn't account for Vial and a curve that averages 2.25 mana. You have 15 blue sources. Cavern makes your Merfolk uncounterable, and Mutavault counts as every creature type, so your Lords pump it.

**Sideboarding**
- **Broodscale Combo and Eldrazi Tron:** bring in all 4 Consign to Memory and Chalice on 1. Consign counters colorless spells, which covers Broodscale, Emrakul and Kozilek's Command, and it also counters combo triggers. Chalice on 1 stops Ancient Stirrings, Springleaf Drum and Vexing Bauble. Take out Snapback and 2–3 Silvergill Adept.
- **Prowess:** Chalice on 1 shuts off Lightning Bolt, Lava Dart, Mishra's Bauble and Cori-Steel Cutter. Consign counters Cutter's triggers. Dismember kills Dragon's Rage Channeler and Slickshot Show-Off. Cut Flare and Snapback.
- **Affinity:** bring in Chalice and Consign (it counters colorless artifact spells) and Dismember.
- **Energy, Zoo and Frog:** Dismember and Subtlety. Tidebinder already handles Phlage and Ragavan triggers.
- **Storm, Goryo's Vengeance, Living End and Devoted Druid:** Force of Negation and Consign. Tidebinder can stop Devoted Druid's untap ability.

**Label and source**
This is **tuned**, not stock. The base is a Modern League list that went 5-0 on 2026-10-13. I swapped 3 Snapback for 3 Tishana's Tidebinder to beat Broodscale Combo, the most played deck. The sideboard keeps that list's core (Chalice, Consign, Force of Negation, Subtlety). I dropped one Force and one Subtlety to make room for 2 Dismember, because aggressive creature decks are a big part of the field.

**What I couldn't verify**
- The Harbinger–Saga interaction above is my reading of the rules.
- The meta tool's data on Merfolk itself is thin, at 14 lists. Matchup claims are my reasoning from the archetype data, not recorded win rates.

results.prompt: Make a fun mono white control deck for Modern leagues.
results.text:
I built and submitted **Mono-White Scepter Superfriends**, a brew. It isn't a copy of any tournament list. I took the deck's skeleton from current UW Control, which runs Isochron Scepter, Orim's Chant, Wrath of the Skies, Solitude, Monumental Henge and Kaheera, and built a mono-white deck around it.

## The plan
Clear the board early with cheap removal and Wrath of the Skies. Then land an **Isochron Scepter** and use it every turn. With **Orim's Chant** on it, your opponent can't cast spells, and if you pay the extra {W} kicker on the copy, they can't attack either. Once they're locked, planeswalkers and creature-making lands win the game.

## Why these cards
- **Isochron Scepter (4):** You put an instant costing 2 or less under it, then pay {2} to cast a free copy whenever you like. You have 13 cards that work with it: Chant, **Get Lost** (kills a creature, enchantment or planeswalker every turn), **Path to Exile**, **Reprieve** (bounces a spell and draws a card), and **March of Otherworldly Light**.
  - Odds of drawing Scepter by turn 5 on the play: 56.6%.
  - Scepter plus any of those instants: 53.1%.
  - Scepter plus Chant specifically: 30.7%.
  - Monumental Henge can dig Scepter up, so your real odds are a bit better.
- **Solitude (4):** Free removal (evoke it by exiling a white card from your hand), or a 5-mana flash lifelinker.
- **Wrath of the Skies (3) and Farewell (1):** Your sweepers. Farewell can exile only creatures and graveyards and leave your Scepters alone. Watch out: Wrath of the Skies with X of 2 or more also destroys your own Scepter and Lion Sash.
- **Planeswalkers:** The Wandering Emperor (3), Elspeth, Storm Slayer (2) and The Eternal Wanderer (1). The fun part is that **Elspeth doubles your tokens**. Castle Ardenvale makes two Humans, and the Emeria's Call spell side makes **four** 4/4 Angels.
- **Lion Sash and Beza:** Lion Sash exiles cards from graveyards (good against Goryo's Vengeance and Living End) and grows into a threat. Beza catches you up on life, cards, creatures or mana.
- **Kaheera, the Orphanguard (companion):** A free extra card. You can use her because every creature in the main deck is an Elemental or a Cat. Kaheera's hybrid cost can be paid with white.

## Mana
23 lands: 17 Plains, 2 Monumental Henge, Castle Ardenvale, Cave of the Frost Dragon, Geier Reach Sanitarium, and Emeria's Call (a spell that can also be played as a land). All but Geier Reach make white.
- Henge and Castle enter untapped as long as you control a Plains.
- Henge's search is strong here because 14 main-deck cards are "historic" (artifacts and legendaries), which is what it finds.
- check_deck passed with no errors. Its only notes were that real UW Control lists run blue and red sources, which doesn't matter for a mono-white deck.

## Sideboarding against the current field
- **Broodscale Combo (14.4%) and Affinity:** Bring in Stony Silence, Pithing Needle (name Urza's Saga or Blade of the Bloodchief) and High Noon.
- **Prowess, Energy, Rakdos Delirium:** Bring in Celestial Purge, Wrath of God and the 4th Get Lost.
- **Goryo's Vengeance, Living End, Murktide:** Bring in Rest in Peace. Celestial Purge also hits Goryo's black and red threats.
- **Storm, Amulet Titan, Eldrazi Tron:** Bring in Damping Sphere, High Noon and Deafening Silence.
- **Watch out:** High Noon, Deafening Silence and Damping Sphere also limit your own Scepter copies, since a copy counts as a spell you cast. Bring them in instead of Scepters, not alongside them.
- **About Kaheera:** Only bring in Elemental, Cat, Nightmare, Dinosaur or Beast creatures. Any other creature means Kaheera isn't available that game. That's why the sideboard has no Kor Firewalker or Ethersworn Canonist.

## What I couldn't verify
- Rules timing I didn't confirm with the tools:
  - Whether you can pay the kicker on a free Scepter copy.
  - Whether Kaheera's restriction is checked again after you sideboard.
- Mono-white Scepter shows up in no recent results, so I can't give you a win rate. It's built for fun in leagues and borrows its removal and mana ideas from proven UW lists.

- **Force of Negation (2):** Free on the opponent's turn and stops any noncreature spell. It's for Doomsday, OmniTell, Storm, Sneak and Show, Tron and Beanstalk.
- **Massacre (2):** Free if the opponent controls a Plains and you control a Swamp. 93% of Ocelot Aggro lists run Plains and 97% run Plateau. Ocelot Aggro (9% of the field) and Death and Taxes (3.5%) together make up about 12.5%. All creatures get -2/-2, so Tamiyo (0/3) survives it but your Bowmasters don't.
- **Barrowgoyf (2):** Deathtouch and lifelink, it gets bigger as card types pile up in graveyards, and it can dig up creatures. It's for the mirror (10.2%, the biggest deck), Ocelot, Izzet Tempo and GX Midrange.
- **Hydroblast (2):** Counters or destroys a red card for one mana. It's for Izzet Tempo and the red cards in Ocelot and Sewer Combo.
- **Nihil Spellbomb (2) + Surgical Extraction (1):** These handle Reanimator (3.8%) and Hogaak (2%). Spellbomb replaces itself if you pay {B}. Surgical can be paid with 2 life and also hits Lands' combo pieces.
- **Sheoldred's Edict (1):** Makes the opponent sacrifice a nontoken creature, a token or a planeswalker. It's good against Eldrazi's big creatures and against the mirror's Kaito.

**Changes from the 5-0 list's sideboard**
- **Cut 4 Leyline of the Void:** Graveyard decks are only about 6% of the field, so I went with cheaper, more flexible graveyard hate.
- **Cut 2 Bloodchief's Thirst:** Swapped for Massacre because of how much Ocelot Aggro there is.
- **Hydroblast:** Went from 1 to 2 copies for Izzet Tempo.

**Sideboard guide** (suggested swaps; adjust for play/draw)
- **Mirror:** +2 Barrowgoyf, +1 Edict; −3 Daze.
- **Ocelot Aggro / Death and Taxes:** +2 Massacre, +2 Barrowgoyf; −4 Daze. They run 4 Wasteland and cheap threats, so Daze gets weaker.
- **Tron:** +3 Consign, +2 Force of Negation; −4 Fatal Push, −1 Brazen Borrower.
- **Eldrazi Aggro:** +3 Consign, +1 Edict, +2 Barrowgoyf; −4 Flow State, −2 Thoughtseize.
- **Doomsday / Storm / OmniTell / Sneak and Show:** +2 Force of Negation, plus Consign against Storm or Hydroblast against Sneak and Show's red cards; −4 Fatal Push, −Bowmasters as needed.
- **Lands:** +3 Consign, +1 Surgical; −4 Fatal Push.
- **Izzet Tempo:** +2 Hydroblast, +2 Barrowgoyf; −Thoughtseize.
- **Reanimator / Hogaak:** +2 Spellbomb, +1 Surgical; −4 Fatal Push.
- **Sewer Combo:** +3 Consign, +2 Hydroblast; −Fatal Push.

**Mana:** check_deck found nothing to change. You have 19 lands, 15 blue sources and 13 black sources, which matches real Dimir Tempo lists (about 18.9 lands on average).

**What I couldn't verify:** I didn't look up the text or colors of opposing cards, like Ocelot Pride, Goblin Bombardment, Sneak Attack or Dark Depths. The calls about what Hydroblast and Consign hit in each matchup rely on how those decks are generally known to work, not on card text I checked. The specific card swaps are my suggestions, not taken from a proven guide.

results.prompt: Build a fast red aggro deck for Pauper.
results.text:
I built **Mono-Red Rally**, which is currently Pauper's main fast red aggro deck. It's 3.5% of the last 30 days of results, and the archetype data has 216 lists from the last 90 days. This is a **stock** list based on the most common cards across those lists. The latest 5-0 Pauper League list is almost the same.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Clockwork Percussionist
- 4 Goblin Bushwhacker
- 4 Goblin Tomb Raider
- 4 Voldaren Epicure
- 4 Burning-Tree Emissary
- 4 Lightning Bolt
- 4 Galvanic Blast
- 2 Chain Lightning
- 1 Fireblast
- 1 End the Festivities
- 4 Rally at the Hornburg
- 3 Experimental Synthesizer
- 3 Reckless Impulse
- 4 Great Furnace
- 14 Mountain

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Cast into the Fire
- 3 Relic of Progenitus
- 2 End the Festivities
- 3 Red Elemental Blast
- 2 Pyroblast
- 2 Smash to Smithereens

**The plan:** Play several cheap creatures early, then make a big hasty attack around turn 2 or 3. You do that with a kicked Goblin Bushwhacker (+1/+0 and haste for your team) or Rally at the Hornburg (two 1/1s, and your Humans gain haste). Burn spells clear blockers or finish the opponent.

**Why the key cards**
- **Burning-Tree Emissary:** When it enters it adds {R}{G}. That lets you cast it plus a kicked Bushwhacker, or several one-drops, in the same turn.
- **Clockwork Percussionist and Goblin Tomb Raider:** Both have haste. Percussionist is an artifact, so it turns on Tomb Raider (+1/+0 and haste while you control an artifact). When Percussionist dies, you exile the top card of your library and can play it.
- **Voldaren Epicure:** Deals 1 damage when it enters and makes a Blood token. The token is an artifact, so it also turns on Tomb Raider.
- **Great Furnace and Experimental Synthesizer:** More artifacts for Tomb Raider and for Galvanic Blast. Galvanic Blast deals 4 damage instead of 2 once you control three artifacts. Synthesizer and Reckless Impulse also give you extra cards to play, so you don't run out of gas.
- **Burn:** 4 Lightning Bolt, 4 Galvanic Blast, 2 Chain Lightning and 1 Fireblast. You can cast Fireblast for free by sacrificing two Mountains, so it can finish a game out of nowhere.

**Mana:** 18 lands, all red (14 Mountain, 4 Great Furnace), which matches the real lists (average 17.9 lands). The average spell costs 1.38. The checker suggested about 19 lands, but I followed the tournament lists and stayed at 18.

**Sideboarding against the top decks**
- **Faeries, Dimir Control, Terror (about 22% of the field together):** Bring in Red Elemental Blast and Pyroblast. Take out Experimental Synthesizer and some Chain Lightning.
- **Affinity:** Bring in Smash to Smithereens (destroys an artifact and deals 3 damage to its controller) and Cast into the Fire. Cast into the Fire can exile an artifact or deal 1 damage to each of two creatures.
- **Madness (16.5%, the biggest deck), Elves, Mono-White Aggro:** Bring in the extra End the Festivities and Cast into the Fire to wipe out x/1 creatures. Against Madness, Relic of Progenitus can also cut off its graveyard plan.
- **Golgari Gardens and other graveyard decks:** Relic of Progenitus.
- **What to cut:** Usually Reckless Impulse, Synthesizer, or Chain Lightning, depending on the matchup.

**What I couldn't confirm:** The meta data shows how many lists play each card, not win rates for each matchup. The sideboard advice comes from how real Rally lists build their sideboards, not from tested results. I'm also assuming the Madness decks are red-based, because the cards they share with this deck (Epicure, Bolt, Fireblast) are red; I didn't look up their full lists. The single Fireblast and 2 Chain Lightning are flexible slots. If you see a lot of creature decks, Gingerbrute or Inventor's Axe are the common swaps.

results.prompt: Build a Pioneer deck around Greasefang, Okiba Boss that isn't the usual list.
results.text:
I built Orzhov Cycling-Fang, a brew. The usual list puts Parhelion II in the graveyard with green self-mill. This one uses vehicles that discard themselves through cycling.

**The plan**
Cycle Detention Chariot for {W} on turn 1 or 2, then cast Greasefang on turn 3. At the start of combat it brings back a 6/6 with haste, and Greasefang's 4 power crews it by itself. When Chariot enters, it exiles one of the opponent's creatures or artifacts. Greasefang sends the vehicle back to your hand at your end step. That's a feature here: you can cycle it again next turn for {W}, draw a card, and repeat. If Greasefang gets answered, Smuggler's Copter and the cycling creatures give you a second, faster way to win.

**Key cards**
- **Detention Chariot (4):** The engine. It cycles for {W}, then comes back each turn as a 6/6 that exiles a blocker while it's out. It's in 0 recent lists.
- **Valor's Flagship (3):** Cycles for {X}{2}{W}, which puts it in the graveyard and makes X 1/1 Pilot tokens that crew as if they had 2 more power. Brought back, it's a 7/7 with flying, first strike and lifelink. That lifelink swings races against Prowess.
- **Parhelion II (2):** Still the biggest hit. It just needs a discard to get into the graveyard, from Bitter Triumph or a Copter loot.
- **Smuggler's Copter (4):** The tool says it's legal in Pioneer, but it shows up in only 3 recent lists. It's a 2-mana flier whose loot discards your stuck vehicles. The loot happens when it attacks, which is after Greasefang's trigger, so it sets up your next turn.
- **Flourishing Fox and Ruthless Sniper:** One-mana creatures that crew Copter. Every cycle grows the Fox. Sniper lets you pay {1} each time you cycle or discard to put a -1/-1 counter on a creature, which is real removal against Prowess.
- **Archfiend of Ifnir (2):** Each time you cycle or discard another card, it puts a -1/-1 counter on every creature the opponent controls. It can also cycle itself for {2}.
- **Interaction:** 4 Thoughtseize, 4 Fatal Push, 3 Bitter Triumph. Bitter Triumph's discard cost doubles as a way to bin Parhelion.

**Honest odds:** You'll have Greasefang plus a Chariot by turn 3 only 22.4% of the time on the play. By turn 4 you'll have Greasefang plus any way to get a vehicle into the graveyard about 46% of the time. Takenuma helps by fetching a creature such as Greasefang back to your hand. This deck is less explosive than the usual one, so Copter and the creatures need to carry the games where the combo doesn't come together.

**Mana**
23 lands, the same count real Greasefang lists use. That's 21 white sources and 18 black. White is heavier because of Fox, Chariot's {W} cycling and Flagship's {W}{W}{W}. The two Desert of the True can cycle away late. The checker warned about 0 green sources compared with normal lists; that's on purpose, since this version drops green.

**Sideboarding** (based on the current meta)
- **Mono-Red and Izzet Prowess (about 22% combined):** Bring in Pest Control, Collective Brutality, the third Archfiend and Doorkeeper Thrull. Take out Thoughtseize and Parhelion. Pest Control also destroys your own Fox and Sniper, so cast it before you deploy them.
- **Golgari Midrange:** Bring in Vanishing Verse and Duress. Take out Sniper.
- **Jund Sacrifice:** Bring in Doorkeeper Thrull (it stops abilities that trigger when artifacts and creatures enter), Vanishing Verse and Soul-Guide Lantern. Take out Thoughtseize.
- **Cauldron and Greasefang mirrors:** Bring in Soul-Guide Lantern and Doorkeeper Thrull. Thrull also turns off your own Chariot's exile, so time it carefully.
- **UW Control:** Bring in Duress, Loran of the Third Path and Collective Brutality. Take out Fatal Push. Temporary Lockdown is for go-wide or cheap-permanent decks, but it also exiles your own permanents with mana value 2 or less.

**What I couldn't check:** Detention Chariot, Valor's Flagship and Archfiend of Ifnir have no recent tournament results, so this shell is untested. The mana is borrowed from proven Greasefang lists. My claims about how well it does against each deck are reasoning, not data.

results.prompt: Make a Vintage artifact aggro deck.
results.text:
I built Sphere Shops, the creature-based Mishra's Workshop deck that plays artifact creatures behind cost-increasing artifacts. It's **tuned** from proven lists.

## The plan
Use fast mana to play a tax piece on turn 1 (Sphere of Resistance, Thorn of Amethyst, Trinisphere or Chalice of the Void). Then add artifact creatures turn after turn while your opponent pays more for every spell and loses lands to Wasteland and Strip Mine. Your clock is the creatures. The tax pieces and land destruction keep your opponent from catching up.

**Why this deck and not Raker Shops:** Raker Shops is the more popular Workshop deck (9.1% of the field vs. 4.0%). It's built around an engine instead (Glaring Fleshraker, 4 Grim Monolith, 4 Sensei's Divining Top, Time Vault, Tezzeret). Sphere Shops is the one that wins by attacking with creatures, so it's the better fit for "artifact aggro."

## Key cards
- **Patchwork Automaton (4):** a 2-mana creature that gets a +1/+1 counter every time you cast an artifact. Ward {2} makes it hard to remove through your own taxes.
- **Scrawling Crawler (4):** each player draws a card in your upkeep, and your opponent loses 1 life for every card they draw. That's a 3/2 body plus steady damage.
- **Stonecoil Serpent (2):** a creature you can cast for any amount, with reach, trample and protection from multicolored.
- **Nettlecyst (2):** comes with its own creature and gets bigger with every artifact you control, which is most of your deck.
- **Lodestone Golem:** a 5/3 that makes all of your opponent's nonartifact spells cost 1 more.
- **Golos (3):** a 3/5 that fetches a land when it enters. With Crucible of Worlds you can replay Wasteland from the graveyard every turn.
- **Tax pieces:** 4 Sphere of Resistance, Thorn of Amethyst, Trinisphere and Chalice of the Void.
- **Null Rod (3):** shuts off the artifact-based mana and engines that the Paradoxical Outcome and Lurrus decks depend on.
- **Card advantage:** Karn, the Great Creator, Mystic Forge and Urza's Saga.

## The mana
- **20 lands**, which matches the archetype average (20.06).
- **Fast-mana count:** 12 cards make extra mana right away: 4 Mishra's Workshop, 4 Ancient Tomb, Mana Crypt, Sol Ring, Black Lotus and Mana Vault. You'll see at least one in your opening 7 cards 80.9% of the time.
- **Colored mana:** the five Moxen, Karakas and Bojuka Bog are your only colored sources. Nothing in the main deck needs colored mana.
- **Land utility:** Ghost Quarter, Petrified Hamlet and Bojuka Bog do jobs beyond making mana.
- The deck checker found no problems with the mana when compared against 79 real Sphere Shops lists.

## Changes from the reference list
The most recent list I found went 2-3 at Vintage Challenge 32, so I adjusted it toward what the archetype plays on average:
- **Main deck:** −1 Nettlecyst (average is 1.9 copies), +1 Petrified Hamlet (played in 58% of lists). Hamlet can name Urza's Saga, Karakas or Tolarian Academy and shut off its abilities.
- **Sideboard:** −1 Leyline of the Void, +1 Mindbreak Trap. Combo decks are a bigger share of the field than Dredge.

## Sideboarding
- **Paradoxical Outcome / Lurrus PO (about 22% of the field):** bring in the 3 Mindbreak Trap. They're free once your opponent casts three spells in a turn, which is how these decks go off. Add Pithing Needle. Take out a Crucible and Golos.
- **Lurrus Control (21%):** bring in the Tabernacle. Making every creature cost {1} each upkeep or die hurts their mana badly when Spheres are also out. Add Grafdigger's Cage, which stops Lurrus recasting cards from the graveyard. Wurmcoil Engine helps in longer games.
- **Mono-White Initiative (12%):** bring in 2 Dismember, 2 Wurmcoil Engine and the second Karakas. Take out Thorn of Amethyst, since their threats are creatures and Thorn doesn't tax those.
- **Dredge and Underworld Breach:** bring in 3 Leyline of the Void and 2 Grafdigger's Cage. Remember that Leyline is only free if it's in your opening hand.
- **Raker Shops and Oath:** for the Shops mirror, use Dismember and Pithing Needle. Grafdigger's Cage stops Oath of Druids from putting creatures onto the battlefield.

## What I couldn't verify
- The share numbers come from the last 30 days of results.
- The specific card swaps are my judgment, based on how often cards appear across the archetype. I haven't tested them.
- I don't have match win rates, so the sideboard plans are reasoned from what each card does, not from results.

results.prompt: Give me a strong Golgari midrange list for Standard.
results.text:
I submitted a legal **Golgari Midrange** deck. It's a **tuned** list: it starts from the Golgari Midrange shell (9 lists in recent results) and moves its creatures toward cards that see a lot more play. One honest warning first: Golgari isn't in the top 20 decks right now, and the most recent Golgari list I found went 1-3 in a Standard Challenge. I built the strongest version I could, but I can't show you a recent winning Golgari list.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Llanowar Elves, 4 Keen-Eyed Curator, 4 Surrak, Elusive Hunter, 3 Qarsi Revenant, 3 Leatherhead, Swamp Stalker, 3 Ouroboroid
- 3 Professor Dellian Fel
- 4 Requiting Hex, 3 Bitter Triumph, 2 Shoot the Sheriff, 2 Maelstrom Pulse, 2 Witherbloom Charm
- 4 Overgrown Tomb, 4 Blooming Marsh, 4 Wastewood Verge, 3 Deathcap Glade, 2 Restless Cottage, 3 Forest, 3 Swamp

**Sideboard (15):** 3 Duress, 2 Strategic Betrayal, 2 Day of Black Sun, 2 Vicious Rivalry, 2 Heritage Reclamation, 2 Cruelclaw's Heist, 1 The Ooze, 1 Maelstrom Pulse

**The plan**
Play big creatures early, using Elves to get ahead on mana. Kill everything cheap with removal that costs 1–2 mana, then win with large tramplers and Professor Dellian Fel. It's a proactive deck that interacts a lot, not a control deck. That matters because the field is mostly creature decks (Jund Sacrifice, Landfall, Boros Dragons, Dimir).

**Why these cards**
- **Surrak (4):** A 4/3 trample for 3 that can't be countered. You draw a card whenever the opponent targets your creatures. It's in about 19.5% of recent lists.
- **Keen-Eyed Curator:** A 3/3 for GG. It exiles graveyard cards for {1}, which fights Reanimator, and it grows to 7/7 trample.
- **Leatherhead:** A 5/4 trampler that enters with a hexproof counter and can destroy an artifact or enchantment when it hits. It's in about 13% of lists.
- **Ouroboroid:** Every combat it puts +1/+1 counters on your whole team, so it takes over a board quickly.
- **Qarsi Revenant:** Flying, deathtouch and lifelink. It blocks dragons and races aggro. Late in the game you can exile it from the graveyard to give those abilities to another creature.
- **Removal:**
  - Requiting Hex (1 mana) kills anything costing 2 or less, which covers most of what Jund Sacrifice plays.
  - Bitter Triumph also hits planeswalkers.
  - Shoot the Sheriff can't hit outlaws (Assassins, Mercenaries, Pirates, Rogues, Warlocks), so it's limited to two copies.
  - Pulse and Witherbloom Charm answer things that aren't creatures.
- **Professor Dellian Fel:** Kills a creature (−3), draws cards (0) or gains 3 life (+2).

**Mana**
- 23 lands plus 4 Elves. The check tool recommended about 23.4 lands for this curve (average mana value 2.51). Real Golgari lists play about 24, but they run Elves less often.
- 22 green sources and 20 black sources, both above the Golgari averages (20.3 green, 18.2 black). That supports the double-green cards (Curator, Ouroboroid, Leatherhead) and Qarsi's double black.
- Restless Cottage gives you a 4/4 attacker late that also exiles graveyard cards.

**Sideboarding**
- **Dimir Midrange / Azorius or 4C Control:**
  - In: Duress, Cruelclaw's Heist, 3rd Pulse.
  - Out: Witherbloom Charm, Shoot the Sheriff, some Requiting Hex.
  - Surrak's card draw punishes their targeted removal.
- **Jund Sacrifice / Landfall:**
  - In: Day of Black Sun, Vicious Rivalry, The Ooze.
  - Out: Bitter Triumph (costs life or a card), slower 4-drops if needed.
  - Keep all four Hex.
- **Boros Dragons:**
  - In: Strategic Betrayal (gets around protection on single big threats).
  - Out: Requiting Hex, since their dragons cost more than 2.
  - Qarsi and Bitter Triumph stay in.
- **Reanimator:**
  - In: Strategic Betrayal (also exiles their graveyard), The Ooze, Heritage Reclamation.
- **Elementals (blue-red spells):**
  - In: Duress, Heist.
  - Out: Hex and Shoot the Sheriff (they play few creatures).
- **Artifacts:**
  - In: Heritage Reclamation, Vicious Rivalry (also destroys artifacts), Pulse.

**What I couldn't verify**
- None of these choices have been tested in matches. They're based on how often cards appear in recent results.
- The Golgari sample is small (9 lists), and there's no win-rate data comparing this list to the stock Golgari builds.

results.prompt: Make a Legacy deck that wins on turn 1 every game.
results.text:
I couldn't build a deck that wins on turn 1 every game, because no such deck exists. Your opening hand is random, so some hands won't have the pieces. Opponents also get free counterspells and turn-1 graveyard hate. Legacy is a 60-card format with no shortcuts around that.

What I built is the closest real option: **Oops All Spells**, a combo deck that tries to win on turn 1 as often as possible.

**Honest odds:** In a 7-card opening hand with no mulligan, you have about a 65% chance to hold a way to start the combo (Balustrade Spy or Lively Dirge). You have about a 33% chance to hold a starter, a Ritual and a free mana card all together. That last figure is only an estimate. Mulligans, the cards that double as lands, and Chrome Mox all change the real number, and the opponent can still stop you after that. Count on a turn-1 win in a meaningful minority of games, a turn-2 win in many more, and some losses to interaction.

**The plan:** The deck has no real lands. Every card that can be played as a land is a spell on its front face, and the front face is what counts while it's in your library. So when Balustrade Spy enters targeting you, it never finds a land and puts your whole library into your graveyard. Each Narcomoeba enters the battlefield as it's milled. You then cast Dread Return from the graveyard by sacrificing three creatures, which costs no mana. It brings back Thassa's Oracle, and with an empty library the Oracle wins the game.

**Why the key cards:**
- **4 Balustrade Spy and 4 Lively Dirge:** these start the combo. For 5 mana, Lively Dirge puts Spy into your graveyard from your library, then returns it to the battlefield, since Spy's mana value is 4.
- **Fast mana:** Lotus Petal, Chrome Mox, Elvish and Simian Spirit Guide, Dark Ritual and Cabal Ritual. Cabal Ritual makes 5 mana once 7 or more cards are in your graveyard.
- **Backup ways to get the Oracle back:** Reanimate, Agadeem's Awakening and Poxwalkers. Bridge from Below makes extra creatures to sacrifice.
- **Protection:** 4 Pact of Negation (a free counterspell; you only pay its 3UU cost on your next upkeep, which doesn't matter if you've already won) and 4 Thoughtseize, plus Cabal Therapy.
- **Memory's Journey:** shuffles cards back into your library so you don't lose by running out of cards if the combo gets stopped partway.

**The mana:** The check tool warned that the deck has "5.5 lands" and should have about 19. I left that alone on purpose. The 11 cards that work as lands (Boggart Trawler, Agadeem's Awakening, Fell the Profane) match the average of 5.5 across the 17 recent lists of this deck. The tool's warning about blue sources doesn't apply either, because you never cast Thassa's Oracle from your hand.

**Sideboard plan:**
- **Graveyard hate (Grafdigger's Cage, Rest in Peace, Leyline of the Void):** bring in Force of Vigor, which you can cast for free by exiling an Elvish Spirit Guide. Wear Down and Foundation Breaker also destroy those cards. Goblin Charbelcher is a second way to win: with no lands in the deck, one activation deals damage equal to your whole library.
- **Counterspell decks (Dimir Tempo 10.2%, Izzet Tempo, OmniTell, Doomsday):** bring in 4 Duress to strip counterspells before you go off.
- **Aggro decks with creatures that tax or stop you (Death and Taxes, Ocelot Aggro):** Fell the Profane is already in the main deck, and Disruptive Stormbrood's cheaper side can destroy a creature with power 3 or less.
- **Cuts:** take out Fell the Profane, a Thoughtseize, or Memory's Journey as needed.

**Label:** Tuned. It's built from the most-played cards across 17 recent Oops All Spells lists, not copied from one finish. The closest reference list went 3-3 in a Legacy Challenge. Oops All Spells isn't in the top 20 by share right now, so it's a real but uncommon deck.

**What I couldn't verify:** The exact chance of winning on turn 1. The odds tool can only check whether certain cards show up in your hand. It can't simulate full combo sequences, mulligans or what the opponent does.

warnings: 5.5 lands; Legacy decks with an average mana value of 2.07 and 14 cheap draw or ramp spells run about 19.3. Add about 14.
11.5 B sources; Agadeem's Awakening // Agadeem, the Undercrypt wants about 23 to cast on curve.
6 U sources; Thassa's Oracle wants about 20 to cast on curve.

results.prompt: Build a Timeless reanimator deck.
results.text:
I built Rakdos (black-red) Reanimator. The deck is accepted and legal in Timeless.

**The plan:** Get a huge creature into your graveyard with Entomb, Faithless Looting or Troll's swampcycling, then bring it back on turn 1 or 2. One fast line: land, Dark Ritual for three black mana, then Entomb plus Reanimate on turn 1. Thoughtseize, Grief and Collective Brutality clear the way first.

**Key cards**
- **Reanimate (4), Persist (4), Necromancy (2):** your 10 ways to bring a creature back. Necromancy can be cast at instant speed, but then the creature only stays until end of turn. Persist only returns nonlegendary creatures, so the creature mix is split on purpose:
  - **Legendary:** Atraxa and Griselbrand. Use Reanimate or Necromancy. Atraxa refills your hand; Griselbrand lets you pay 7 life to draw 7.
  - **Nonlegendary, so Persist works:** Sire of Seven Deaths (7/7 with lifelink, and removal costs the opponent 7 life), Troll of Khazad-dûm, and Grief.
- **Troll of Khazad-dûm:** For 1 mana it swampcycles into the graveyard and finds you a land at the same time. It's a 6/5 that can't be blocked except by three or more creatures.
- **Grief:** Evoke it for free for a discard effect, then Persist or Reanimate it to make the opponent discard again and keep a 3/2 menace.
- **Entomb (4), Faithless Looting (4):** your main ways to get a creature into the graveyard. Brutality can also discard one as an extra cost.

**Odds:** On the play, you'll see at least one way to fill your graveyard by turn 2 in 85% of games, a reanimation spell in 79%, and both in 66% (no mulligans counted).

**The mana:** 16 lands plus 2 Chrome Mox and 4 Dark Ritual. Every land makes black mana, and you have 10 red sources for Looting. The fetch lands can grab Blood Crypt since it counts as a Swamp. The deck checker warned I should run about 22 lands, but that number assumes you'll pay for the 7- and 8-mana creatures, which you never do. Legacy Reanimator lists average 14.6 lands, so 16 is already on the safe side.

**Sideboarding:** There's no Timeless tournament data, so the sideboard is aimed at common threats in general.
- **Against counterspells:** Bring in Hexing Squelcher (3) and Duress (3). Squelcher stops your spells from being countered and gives your other creatures "Ward—Pay 2 life." Take out Brutality and some Thoughtseize.
- **Against graveyard hate:** Kolaghan's Command and Abrade destroy artifacts like Tormod's Crypt. Command can also return a creature card from your graveyard to your hand.
- **Against fast creature decks:** Bring in Fatal Push and Abrade; trim Grief.
- **Against other graveyard decks:** Leyline of the Void. It only exiles the opponent's cards, so it doesn't hurt you.
- **Against greedy multicolor mana:** Blood Moon. Your four Swamps keep working under it.

**Label:** It's a **brew**. The tool had no Timeless results, so I took the structure and mana ideas from Legacy Reanimator. That list doesn't work as-is here, because these Legacy staples came back as not legal in Timeless: Animate Dead, Lotus Petal, Unmask, Cabal Therapy, Shallow Grave, Exhume, Goryo's Vengeance, Archon of Cruelty, Underground Sea, Badlands, Stronghold Gambit and Pyroblast.

**Couldn't verify:**
- The current Timeless meta, so the sideboard isn't tuned to specific decks.
- Timeless's restricted list. The legality check accepted 4 copies of Entomb and Thoughtseize, but if your client says otherwise, use Unmarked Grave (finds Sire, Troll or Grief) and Duress instead.

You win by attacking with a wide board of creatures that your lords have made bigger. If that doesn't finish it, Shaman of the Pack drains them for big chunks of life, or you fetch Craterhoof Behemoth to give your whole team a large boost for one lethal attack.

- 4 Elvish Clancaller, 4 Leaf-Crowned Visionary, 4 Elvish Warmaster
- 4 Elvish Archdruid, 3 Priest of Titania
- 4 Shaman of the Pack, 1 Craterhoof Behemoth

Then win slowly with Serra Angel, Mishra's Factory and Triskelion. Moat stops creatures without flying from attacking, but Serra flies, and the deck's few attackers can get past it.

Hasty creatures and creatures that deal damage when they enter take the first 8–10 points. Then 22 burn spells finish the opponent from about 6 life. Use the burn on blockers early only if it keeps your creatures attacking. Otherwise, aim it at the opponent's face.

**What's missing**
Penny Dreadful only allows cheap cards, and the classic burn cards are all banned right now. I checked: Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning, Lava Spike, Rift Bolt, Skewer the Critics, Monastery Swiftspear, Goblin Guide, Eidolon of the Great Revel, Fireblast, Skullcrack, Lightning Helix and Boros Charm. Without Helix and Boros Charm there's no reason to add white, so the deck is mono-red.

**Key cards**
- **Burst Lightning and Shock:** your 1-mana burn, 2 damage each. Burst Lightning can pay an extra 4 mana for 4 damage later in the game.
- **Lightning Strike and Searing Spear:** 3 damage for 2 mana, at instant speed.
- **Exquisite Firecraft:** 4 damage for 3 mana. Once you have two instants or sorceries in your graveyard, it can't be countered.
- **Keldon Marauders:** 1 damage when it enters and 1 when it leaves, plus a 3/3 body that attacks once or twice. That usually adds up to 5–7 damage.
- **Viashino Pyromancer:** 2 damage to the opponent when it enters, and it still attacks.
- **Hellspark Elemental:** a 3/1 with trample and haste. You can bring it back from the graveyard once for 2 more mana, so it hits twice.
- **Fervent Champion:** a 1-mana attacker with first strike and haste.
- **Bonecrusher Giant:** cast its Stomp half first for 2 damage, then cast the 4/3 creature later.
- **Sulfuric Vortex:** deals 2 damage to each player at the start of their turn and stops all lifegain. Only 2 copies, because it hurts you too.

**The mana**
19 lands, all red: 17 Mountain and 2 Castle Embereth. Castle Embereth enters untapped if you have a Mountain and can pump your creatures late. The checker flagged 19 lands as low and suggested about 23. I kept 19 on purpose: the most expensive card costs 3 and the deck averages under 2 mana per card. **Sideboarding**
I had no meta data, so this is aimed at the kinds of decks you'd expect to face:
- **Wide token or creature decks:** bring in Pyroclasm and Mizzium Mortars. Take out Sulfuric Vortex and some Fervent Champions.
- **Artifact decks:** bring in Smash to Smithereens, which destroys an artifact and deals 3 to its owner. Take out Shock.
- **Lifegain decks:** bring in Rampaging Ferocidon, which stops lifegain and pings creature decks. Take out Bonecrusher Giant.
- **Decks with lots of multicolor lands:** bring in Price of Progress.
- **Decks that activate abilities a lot (equipment, creatures, utility lands):** bring in Harsh Mentor.
- **Graveyard decks:** bring in Ash Zealot.

**Caveats**

results.prompt: Combine Living End and Scam into one Modern deck.
results.text:
I built a Bant (green-blue-white) Living End deck that uses the evoke elementals as its Scam half. It's a brew. Before the list, two problems with the request.

**Why it isn't classic Scam**
- **The original Scam creatures are banned.** The card lookup shows **Grief and Fury as banned in Modern**, so the turn-1 discard version of Scam can't be built. Solitude, Subtlety and Endurance are legal.
- **The cheap save spells don't work in this deck.** Ephemerate, Not Dead After All, Feign Death and Malakir Rebirth (all 1 mana) would break cascade. Shardless Agent costs 3, so its cascade casts the first card it reveals that costs less than 3. Right now Living End (cost 0) is the deck's only spell under 3, so every cascade finds it. Add four of those 1-drops and each cascade could hit a dead spell instead. That would ruin the main plan.

**How the two halves fit together**
- **Classic Scam turn, done at 4 mana:** evoke Solitude (free by exiling a white card from your hand). While its triggers are on the stack, flash in **Restoration Angel** (costs 4) and blink Solitude. It comes back as a new creature and stays. You get two exile triggers, a 3/2 lifelinker and a 3/4 flyer. It's a turn later than real Scam, but it costs 4, so cascade can never hit it.
- **Living End as the mass version:** every elemental you evoke early ends up in your graveyard. When you cascade into Living End on turn 3, they all come back at once. Solitude's exile and Endurance's graveyard shuffle trigger again on the way back.

**The plan:** use evoked elementals as free interaction on turns 1–3 while landcycling and cycling creatures into the graveyard. Then cascade into Living End and swing with a full board. If that gets stopped, the Restoration Angel line is a second, fairer way to win.

**Key cards**
- **4 Shardless Agent and 4 Ardent Plea:** these are the cascade cards. You have a 75.1% chance of drawing one by turn 3 on the play, before mulligans. Ardent Plea replaces Violent Outburst, so the deck needs no red, and it counts as a white card for Solitude. The cost is losing the instant-speed cascade.
- **Elementals (4 Solitude, 4 Subtlety, 4 Endurance, 2 Wistfulness):** free interaction early and creatures for Living End later.
- **Free-spell fuel:** 14 white cards for Solitude, 19 blue cards for Subtlety and Force of Negation, and 14 green cards for Endurance.
- **Graveyard fillers:** 4 Street Wraith, 4 Generous Ent and 3 Eagles of the North. Eagles fetches a Plains-type land (Plains, Temple Garden, Hallowed Fountain, Lush Portico, Meticulous Archive), counts as a white card for Solitude, and gives your team first strike after a Living End.
- **4 Force of Negation:** protects the combo.

**Mana:** 16 lands plus Sink into Stupor, which can be played as a land, close to real Living End lists (15.6 on average). All 6 fetchlands can find a land of any of your three colors. Ent and Eagles also find lands. `check_deck` counted only 7 white sources because it doesn't count fetchlands. It also flagged 0 red sources compared with real lists; that's on purpose, since the deck plays no red cards.

**Sideboard**

Every sideboard card costs 3 or more, so none of them break cascade. That's why I left out Inevitable Betrayal and Damping Sphere, even though Living End lists normally play them.
- **Broodscale Combo (14.4%), Devoted Druid, Affinity:** bring in 3 Clarion Conqueror, 2 Force of Vigor and 2 Foundation Breaker. Take out Eagles, Restoration Angel and Sink.
- **Prowess and Energy:** bring in 2 Dismember, plus Clarion Conqueror against Energy. Take out Force of Negation and Sink. Solitude and Endurance are your early defense.
- **Blue decks and counterspells (Blink, Frog, Goryo's, UW Control):** bring in 4 Mystical Dispute and 2 Teferi, Time Raveler. Take out Eagles and Wistfulness.
- **Eldrazi Tron:** bring in Dismember and Teferi.

**What I couldn't verify**
- Ardent Plea, Eagles of the North and Restoration Angel show zero recent tournament lists, so those slots are untested.
- The format data doesn't list Scam as a current deck, so there was no proven list to borrow its mana from.

results.text:

This comes from a recent 5-0 Pauper League list (2026-10-11). Kiln Fiend already has its own archetype in Pauper, with 9 lists in the last 90 days. You asked for a deck built around the card, so the proven list is the right answer. I didn't change anything.

**Main deck (60)**

- 2 Relic of Progenitus

**The plan**
You play a creature that gets bigger every time you cast an instant or sorcery. Then you cast a burst of cheap or free spells and give it double strike. One big attack wins the game.

For example: Kiln Fiend, then Rite of Flame, Manamorphose, Mutagenic Growth and Temur Battle Rage. That's four spells, so it gets +12 power, plus +2 from Growth, for 15 power. It hits twice with trample, for 30 damage.

**Why these cards**
- **Kiln Fiend** (2 mana, 1/2) gets +3/+0 for each instant or sorcery you cast. **Festival Crasher** and **Ghitu Amplifier** do the same thing at +2/+0. That's 12 threats, so you have about an 85% chance to see one by turn 2 on the play.
- **Free or mana-neutral spells:**
  - **Mutagenic Growth** and **Apostle's Blessing** can be paid for with life instead of mana.
  - **Manamorphose** gives back its two mana and draws a card.
  - **Rite of Flame** costs 1 and makes 2 red.
  - **Lava Dart** can be cast a second time by sacrificing a Mountain.
  
  Each of these is one more spell that pumps your creature.
- **Protection:** Apostle's Blessing gives your threat protection from a color (or from artifacts) in response to removal. Mutagenic Growth can also save it from damage-based removal.
- **Finishers:** You have 7 double-strike spells (4 Temur Battle Rage, 3 Assault Strobe). Temur Battle Rage also gives trample once your creature has 4 or more power. Crash Through gives trample and draws a card. You have about a 74% chance to see a double-strike spell by turn 4.

**Mana**
17 Mountains, with all 17 producing red, the same as every recent list. The deck checker suggested about 18.4 lands. I'm trusting the tournament lists here, because Rite of Flame, Manamorphose and the life-paid spells make up for the missing land.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Madness** (16.5% of the field, the most-played deck): Relic of Progenitus against its graveyard plan. Electrickery for small creatures.
- **Faeries, Terror, Dimir Control, Jeskai Control:** Red Elemental Blast counters their blue spells or destroys a blue permanent. Electrickery cast for its overload cost wipes out Faeries' 1-toughness flyers.
- **Affinity:** Raze the Effigy destroys an artifact. In the deck it can also give an attacking creature +2/+2 and counts as another spell. Molten Rain hits their artifact lands.
- **Tron:** Molten Rain on Tron lands.
- **Elves, Mono-White Aggro:** Electrickery.
- **Bogles, Mono-White, Spy Combo:** Flaring Pain stops their damage-prevention tricks from blanking your big attack. It's played heavily in Bogles and Spy Combo lists, which suggests that's the effect it answers. That's my inference, not something the data says.
- **What to cut:** Usually Assault Strobe or Lava Dart. Keep at least 12 creatures and about 6 double-strike effects.

**Honest odds**
You'll have both Kiln Fiend itself and a double-strike spell by turn 4 only about 38% of the time. You'll often be winning with Crasher or Amplifier instead, which is why the deck runs 12 creatures. The deck is also fragile against blockers with high toughness and against instant-speed removal when you don't have Blessing. Mulligan hands that have no creature.

**What I couldn't verify**
My data only covers 9 recent lists of this deck, so it doesn't show its win rate against specific matchups.

results.prompt: Build me a Premodern Dream Halls deck that doesn't win with storm.
results.text:
I built **Blue-Red Dream Halls with a Seismic Assault kill**. It has no Brain Freeze or any other storm card. This is a **brew**. Its base comes from the stock Dream Halls deck (10 recent Premodern lists), but every one of those lists runs Brain Freeze, and nobody is posting results with this exact version.

## The plan
Put Dream Halls into play early. Ancient Tomb, City of Traitors, Svyelunite Temple and Lotus Petal can get you the 5 mana. Show and Tell puts it in for free. Once it's out, you cast spells by discarding a card that shares a color instead of paying mana. Chain the big draw spells, cast Seismic Assault the same way, then discard every land you drew at 2 damage each. Prophetic Bolt adds 4 damage each, and Fire adds 2.

## Why these cards
- **Seismic Assault (3)**: "Discard a land card: 2 damage to any target." Dream Halls can't make you discard lands, because lands have no color. So every land you draw during the chain becomes ammunition. It also kills Goblins and Sligh creatures.
- **Gush (3)**: You can cast it by returning two Islands to your hand. That's two cards drawn plus two more lands to discard to Seismic Assault. This is why the deck runs 9 basic Islands.
- **Prophetic Bolt (3) and Fire // Ice (2)**: These are blue and red, so they can be cast with Dream Halls by discarding a blue card. They can also be discarded to cast either Seismic Assault or your blue spells. Prophetic Bolt is 4 damage plus card selection.
- **Draw spells**:
  - Meditate draws 4. Skipping your next turn doesn't matter, because you win that turn.
  - Opportunity draws 4.
  - Rush of Knowledge draws 5, since Dream Halls is 5 mana value.
- **Finding the pieces**: Intuition finds Dream Halls, or a pile of three Seismic Assaults. You'll see Dream Halls or Intuition by turn 4 about 74% of the time (going first, no mulligans). Sleight of Hand and Frantic Search smooth your draws, and Arcane Denial protects the combo.

## Mana
The deck has 19 lands, which matches the average of real Dream Halls lists (19.1). It has 16 blue sources, against their average of 16.4. The deck checker gave two warnings, and both are fine:
- **It wants about 24 lands.** That rule doesn't fit a deck that cheats on mana with Dream Halls.
- **It wants about 23 red sources for Seismic Assault.** That's for casting it with RRR, which you almost never do. The only red mana you need is the two Shivan Reefs and the Petals, for casting Fire before the combo.

## Sideboarding (based on the current field)
- **Sligh and Goblins:** Bring in 2 Blue Elemental Blast, 2 Hydroblast and Powder Keg. Take out Show and Tell and Arcane Denial. Seismic Assault doubles as removal here.
- **Stiflenought, UB Psychatog and Standstill:** Bring in 3 Defense Grid, Stifle and Annul (Annul counters Phyrexian Dreadnought). Take out Frantic Search and Fire // Ice. Don't fire Show and Tell into an opponent with Dreadnought in hand.
- **Enchantress:** Bring in 2 Annul and 2 Chain of Vapor. Take out Arcane Denial and 1 Fire // Ice.
- **Hermit Druid and Replenish:** Bring in 2 Tormod's Crypt, Stifle and Annul. Take out Sleight of Hand.
- **Terrageddon:** The cheap mana is your edge, so try to set up the combo before Armageddon. Defense Grid helps if they have countermagic.

## Things to know
- The kill isn't guaranteed. You need roughly 10 lands in hand (or fewer plus Bolts) after chaining. My estimate is that a full chain gets there through land draws and Gush returns. I haven't simulated this, though.
- With no storm card, there's no backup kill if the lands run short.

- Brainstorm is banned in Premodern, so Sleight of Hand takes its place.

results.prompt: Build a deck that best utilizes Peter Parker's Camera.
results.text:
I built this for Standard, because that's where the Camera is legal and where its best partners are. The Camera costs {1} and enters with three film counters. Each activation costs {2}, taps it, removes a counter, and copies an activated or triggered ability you control, with new targets if you want. That works best in a deck full of strong abilities, and Azorius (white-blue) Artifacts is exactly that deck: 4.7% of the current field and the only strategy where the Camera has shown up in results (one list).

**The plan**
You play a pile of cheap artifacts that each do something when they enter, plus Repurposing Bay to trade them up the mana curve. The Camera turns your best ones into two-for-ones. You win with Construct tokens from Simulacrum Synthesizer and Doombots from Castle Doom while your artifacts exile the opponent's threats.

**Best things to copy**
- **Repurposing Bay:** {2}, tap, sacrifice another artifact to put an artifact costing exactly 1 more from your library onto the battlefield. Respond to its activation with the Camera and you should get two artifacts for one. For example, sacrifice a 3-mana artifact and get both White Auracite and The Fire Crystal. Once the Camera runs out of film, it's a 1-mana artifact you can sacrifice to Bay to fetch a 2-drop.
- **Perilous Snare and White Auracite:** each exiles an opponent's nonland permanent until it leaves. A copy exiles a second one.
- **Spring-Loaded Sawblades:** the copy deals 5 damage to a second tapped creature.
- **Others:** the copy also works on Castle Doom (a second 3/3 Doombot without sacrificing again), Synthesizer's Construct trigger, Cryogen Relic's draw, and Clay-Fired Bricks (a second Plains).
- **Tezzeret, Cruel Captain (1 copy):** its −3 can find the Camera, since it searches for an artifact costing 1 or less. Copying that −3 gets you two artifacts. Its 0 untaps the Camera, so you can use it twice in a turn.
- **United Battlefront** can also put the Camera onto the battlefield, since it takes noncreature permanents costing 3 or less.
- **Odds:** you'll see a Camera, Battlefront or Tezzeret by turn 4 about 83% of the time. You'll have both a Camera and one of the 12 best copy targets by turn 5 about 52% of the time.

**Changes from the 5-0 Standard League reference list**
- In: 4 Camera, 1 Tezzeret, 1 more White Auracite (a second 4-mana target for Bay).
- Out: 3 Candy Trail (the Camera takes over its slot as a 1-mana artifact to sacrifice), 2 Boomerang Basics, 1 main-deck Day of Judgment (it kills your own Constructs; it moved to the sideboard).
- I kept everything else. That core shows up in about 85–97% of the 93 lists, and the Camera needs exactly those artifacts to copy.

**Mana**
23 lands, the same as the reference list, with 18 white and 17 blue sources. The deck checker flagged that The Fire Crystal wants red. That's fine: you'll usually put it onto the battlefield with Bay rather than cast it, and Castle Doom's any-color mana can pay for it if you do. Keep {2} open after your main play so the Camera can respond to Bay at instant speed.

**Sideboarding**
- **Jund Sacrifice, Elementals, Boros Dragons, Prowess:** bring in Day of Judgment, the extra Authority of the Consuls and Torpor Orb. Orb also shuts off their creature enter triggers; your artifact triggers still work.
- **Landfall:** bring in Torpor Orb and the extra Authority of the Consuls.
- **Reanimator, Lessons:** bring in Rest in Peace.
- **Dimir Midrange and the control decks:** bring in No More Lies, Voice of Victory, Krang, Astelli Reclaimer and the 4th Starcage. Take out Day of Judgment and Erode.

**Label:** tuned. It's a proven list rebuilt around the Camera.

**What I couldn't verify:** my tools don't cover rulings. I'm assuming a copy of Bay's ability uses the mana value of the artifact sacrificed for the original, which is how copied costs normally work, but confirm it before you rely on the double fetch. Gogo, Master of Mimicry is another blue card that copies abilities, but it hasn't been played in any results, so I left it out.

results.prompt: Build a Commander deck with Atraxa, Praetors' Voice that's all about proliferate.
results.text:
I built a brew called **Atraxa Superfriends Proliferate** and the site accepted it as a legal 100-card deck (Atraxa plus 99).

**The plan**
The deck plays planeswalkers and then keeps adding counters to them. Atraxa proliferates at your end step, and about 22 other cards in the deck also proliferate. Every proliferate adds loyalty to all your planeswalkers, so they reach their ultimates much sooner. It can also grow +1/+1 counters and drain opponents.

You can win four ways:
- **Planeswalker ultimates:** extra turns from Teferi, Master of Time, a free-spells emblem from Tamiyo, or Vraska, Golgari Queen's emblem.
- **Poison:** Vraska, Betrayal's Sting's −9 brings a player to nine poison counters. One more proliferate takes them to 10, which kills.
- **Drain:** Scheming Aspirant makes each opponent lose 2 life every time you proliferate.
- **Combat:** Atraxa attacks in the air.

**Why the key cards**
- **Proliferate engines:**
  - Evolution Sage proliferates on every land drop, and each fetch land counts twice.
  - Flux Channeler and Inexorable Tide proliferate whenever you cast spells.
  - Ichormoon Gauntlet gives every planeswalker "0: Proliferate" and a −12 extra turn.
  - Karn's Bastion is a land that proliferates.
  - Expansion Algorithm proliferates X times.
  - Brokers Confluence is an instant that can proliferate three times.
- **Doublers:**
  - Tekuthal makes every proliferate happen twice.
  - Doubling Season, Vorinclex and Innkeeper's Talent (level 3) double counters you put on things, including loyalty. Vorinclex and Innkeeper's Talent also double poison on players.
  - Deepglow Skate doubles the counters already on your permanents when it enters.
- **Payoffs:** Ezuri draws a card every time you proliferate, and Scheming Aspirant drains. Oath of Teferi lets each planeswalker use an ability twice per turn.
- **Removal that also proliferates:** Atomize, Drown in Ichor and Fuel for the Cause.
- **Board wipes:** Toxic Deluge and Supreme Verdict only kill creatures, so your planeswalkers survive them.
- **Protection:** Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention and Mutational Advantage.

**Odds**
I checked the odds with 23 proliferate cards, before I cut Vivisurgeon's Insight. At that count you have about a 94% chance to see at least one by turn 4 on the play, and a 74% chance to see one of the 12 planeswalkers. With 22 the first number is a little lower.

**The mana**
- There are 36 lands, mostly multicolor: shock lands, fetch lands, four three-color lands that enter tapped (triomes) and some lands that produce any color.
- 10 ramp pieces: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, Birds of Paradise, Noble Hierarch, Bloom Tender, Farseek, Nature's Lore, Three Visits and Cultivate. Wrenn and Realmbreaker also fixes colors.
- Color sources: 20 white, 23 blue, about 21 black and 22 green.

**Warnings from the deck check**
- **Lands:** it suggested about 38.6 lands. I kept 36 because there are 10 ramp cards and a lot of cheap card draw.
- **Expansion Algorithm:** it said Expansion Algorithm wants more blue sources. Its cost is X plus two blue, so it's meant as a big late-game spell, not something you need on curve.

**Sideboarding**
Commander has no sideboard, and the tools had no tournament data for this format. Instead, the deck covers common problems in the main deck:
- **Big creature decks:** two wipes, Swords to Plowshares and Path to Exile.
- **Combo and big spells:** Counterspell and Fuel for the Cause.
- **Artifacts and enchantments:** Assassin's Trophy, Anguished Unmaking and Beast Within.
- **Wide boards:** a full Cyclonic Rift.

If your group plays a lot of fliers, consider Vraska the Unseen or Vivien Reid. If you face a lot of countermagic, consider Reject Imperfection.

**Label**
This is a **brew**. There was no tournament data for Atraxa or Commander to borrow from, so I built it from card searches. The mana is a standard four-color setup I put together myself, not one copied from a proven list.

**What I couldn't verify**
- Card prices, so this assumes no budget limit. The fetches, shocks, Doubling Season, Jace and Oko are expensive. Cheaper swaps:
  - Fetches and shocks → more triomes and check lands.
  - Doubling Season → Pir, Imaginative Rascal.
- Your playgroup's power level. If they don't like extra-turn and free-spell ultimates, drop Teferi, Master of Time and Tamiyo for more counter-focused planeswalkers.
