results.prompt: Build an aggressive Duel Commander deck with a red commander.
results.text:
I built **Mono-Red Aggro with Zurgo Bellstriker as commander**. It's a stock list: the most recent top finish for this deck, a 5-0 Duel Commander League run dated 2026-09-13. It passed the deck check with no errors or warnings.

**The plan**
Play cheap, hasty creatures on turns 1 and 2, use about 25 burn spells to clear blockers, then point the rest at your opponent's face to finish. The average mana value is 1.87. Thirty cards cost 1 mana and 21 cost 2, so most turns you can cast two spells.

**Why Zurgo**
Of the red commanders I checked, Zurgo is the most purely aggressive one with recent results. He costs one red mana for a 2/2. His Dash cost ({1}{R}) gives him haste and returns him to your hand at end of turn, which keeps him safe from sorcery-speed removal and avoids the commander tax. Other red options exist, but they play differently:
- **Magda, Brazen Outlaw** (9 lists in the last 90 days) is a slower Dwarves-and-Treasure artifact deck.
- **Aragorn, King of Gondor** is red, white and blue, but its stock build is mostly counterspells.

**Key cards**
- **Fast hasty threats:** Goblin Guide, Monastery Swiftspear, Slickshot Show-Off (flying and haste, +2/+0 for each noncreature spell you cast) and Screaming Nemesis (haste; whenever it's dealt damage, it deals that much damage to any other target, and a player hit this way can't gain life for the rest of the game).
- **Free spells for an explosive turn:** Fireblast (sacrifice two Mountains to deal 4 to any target), Pyrokinesis (exile a red card from your hand to deal 4 damage divided among creatures) and Fury (can be evoked for free; deals 4 damage divided among creatures and planeswalkers).
- **Burn:** Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning and the rest double as removal early and as reach late.
- **Eidolon of the Great Revel:** it deals 2 damage to any player who casts a spell with mana value 3 or less. Your deck handles that tax better than slower decks do.

**The mana**
The deck runs 36 lands: 25 Snow-Covered Mountains and 11 other lands, all of which make red. That's 3 fewer than the checker's general recommendation (39.5), but it matches real Zurgo lists (average 36.33). With a curve this low, fewer lands is correct.
- The six fetch lands make Fireblast easier to cast, since they find Mountains to sacrifice.
- Some lands do extra work. Barbarian Ring, Ramunap Ruins (2 damage to each opponent) and Shinka add damage. Sokenzan can make creatures at instant speed. Arena of Glory can give a creature haste.

**Sideboarding**
I didn't build a 15-card sideboard. I'm assuming tournament Duel Commander is played without one: the winning list had nothing in it besides the commander itself. How to approach the current field:
- **Cloud, Midgar Mercenary (top deck at 11.3%):** Cloud is a 2/1 that costs two white mana and searches up Equipment when it enters. Kill it with Shock, Burst Lightning or Wild Slash before it gets equipped. Its whole engine needs Cloud to be equipped.
- **Counterspell-heavy decks (Jace, Aragorn):** play threats one at a time, and lean on Dash, Slickshot's plot and the creature-making lands so a counterspell doesn't cost you much. Save burn to finish at instant speed.
- **Bigger midrange decks (Tasigur, Winter):** race them, and use the free spells to have a big turn before their larger creatures stabilize the board.

**What I couldn't verify**
- I didn't look up the rules text of every card. I checked Zurgo, Fury, Screaming Nemesis, Fireblast, Eidolon, Arena of Glory, Cori-Steel Cutter, Goblin Guide, Slickshot, Pyrokinesis and Ramunap Ruins. I didn't check the text of Barbarian Ring, Shinka or Sokenzan, so what I said about them is from memory, not from a lookup.
- Zurgo appears in only 3 lists over the last 90 days. That's a small sample, so treat the build as proven but not heavily tuned.
- The no-sideboard rule is an assumption. If your event allows one, add more cheap removal for the Cloud matchup.

results.prompt: Something weird but competitive for Premodern.
results.text:
I built you **Aluren** (4-color Survival combo). It's weird: one enchantment lets you cast your creatures for free at instant speed, and you win by bouncing the same few creatures over and over. It's also competitive: the archetype tool found 19 results for it, and the list I started from went 5-0 in a Premodern League. Aluren only makes up about 1.3% of the current field, so most opponents won't have practiced against it.

**The plan**
Find **Aluren** or **Survival of the Fittest**, then go off in one turn. Aluren lets any player cast creatures with mana value 3 or less for free, as though they had flash.
- **Cavern Harpy** enters and returns **Man-o'-War** to your hand. Recast Man-o'-War for free and use it to return **Ghitu Slinger**. Recast the Slinger to deal 2 damage.
- Pay 1 life to return the Harpy to your hand, then do it again.
- When your life gets low, put **Spike Feeder** in the loop instead of the Slinger. You can remove its two counters for 2 life each, so 4 life per cast, and each loop only costs 1. That means you can repeat the loop as many times as you need.
- **Raven Familiar** loops the same way with the Harpy and looks at your top 3 cards each time, to dig for whatever piece is missing.
- Echo never matters, because the creatures go back to your hand before your next upkeep.

**Why the key cards**
- **Survival of the Fittest** turns any spare creature into the combo piece you need.
- **Academy Rector** can be found with Survival. When it dies (you can sacrifice it to **Cabal Therapy**'s flashback), it puts an enchantment from your library onto the battlefield, usually Aluren.
- **Monk Realist** destroys an enchantment when it enters. That's your answer to Enchantress's **Solitary Confinement** (with it out, the Slinger's damage can't reach them) and to anything else that stops you.
- **Squee** gives Survival a creature to discard every turn, since it comes back from the graveyard to your hand. **Whirlpool Rider** reshuffles a bad hand into new cards.
- You have 8 copies of Aluren plus Survival. The odds of seeing at least one by turn 4 on the play, with no mulligans, are **79%**.

**The mana**
23 lands with 4-color fixing: Yavimaya Coast, City of Brass, Gemstone Mine, Llanowar Wastes and Reflecting Pool. **Havenwood Battleground** can be sacrificed for GG to cast Aluren a turn early. **Birds of Paradise** and **Wall of Roots** also speed it up. check_deck counts 24.5 green, 12.5 blue and 11.5 black sources, in line with real Aluren lists, with no warnings.

**Sideboarding**
- **Enchantress (12.5%):** bring in 3 Naturalize and 3 Xantid Swarm. They destroy Solitary Confinement, and Swarm's attack means they can't cast spells (like **Seal of Cleansing**) on the turn you combo. Monk Realist from the main deck also helps.
- **Terrageddon (11.2%):** bring in 2 Tsabo's Web to keep their Wasteland and Rishadan Port tapped. Bring in 2 Hydroblast for their sideboard **Pyroclasm**. Try to combo before Armageddon.
- **Stiflenought, Psychatog, Standstill:** bring in Xantid Swarm against counterspells, plus Tsabo's Web against Port and Wasteland. Bring in Compost and the 4th Cabal Therapy against the black decks.
- **Sligh / Goblins:** bring in Hydroblast. Spike Feeder helps keep your life up.
- **Hermit Druid, Replenish:** bring in 3 Tormod's Crypt.

**Brew, stock or tuned?** **Tuned.** The main deck is the 5-0 League list, unchanged. It already covers the top decks, with Monk Realist against Enchantress. I only changed the sideboard:
- Cut 1 Tormod's Crypt and Gaea's Blessing.
- Added 2 Hydroblast, because red decks (Sligh, Goblins, and Terrageddon's Pyroclasm) are a big part of the field.

**Things to know and what I couldn't verify**
- Aluren works for your opponent too. Goblins, Sligh and other cheap-creature decks get free, flash creatures while it's out, so only cast it when you can win that turn or the same turn.
- The tools didn't tell me exactly what Gaea's Blessing was doing in the original sideboard, so cutting it is my call.
- The matchup notes come from the meta tool's lists of what those decks play, not from tested win rates.
